Option set bounded to always_allow / ask / always_deny — no expansion permitted. RBiH historical default = always_deny per documented ARBiH chain-of-command discipline (UN A/54/549 §35; Hadzihasanovic/Kubura IT-01-47). The always_allow counterfactual carries a steep international-standing floor per Gate §3 #5 (no atrocity-efficiency surface). war_crimes_events increments are produced by the existing paramilitary_sweep engine path on each capture, not by this decision event.

title: What Is Herceg-Bosna?
narrative: Zagreb is on the line. Your patron's directive is clear: Herceg-Bosna exists to secure Croat territory in Bosnia, with a view toward eventual unification with Croatia. But on the ground, your HVO fights alongside the ARBiH against Serb forces. Some of your commanders — notably Kljuic — argue the Croat future lies in a unified Bosnia, not a separate statelet. Your patron disagrees. Choose your path: it will define your alliances, your wars, and your fate at the negotiating table.

effect.text: The political direction of Herceg-Bosna is debated.

source_note: Kordic and Prlic judgments, plus Zagreb meeting and Kljuic-removal context, ground Herceg-Bosna's separatist political project.
staff_assessment: Herceg-Bosna leadership gains patron alignment and clearer institutional cohesion by following Zagreb, but the choice makes cooperation with Sarajevo more fragile.
trigger_evidence: Zagreb's directive and Herceg-Bosna institutions are already shaping HVO policy.
HVO and ARBiH forces still share anti-VRS fronts, making the political direction operationally urgent.

response_options.label: Croat republic — follow Zagreb
response_options.description: Herceg-Bosna is a Croat political entity. We will control our territory along the old Banovina borders. Zagreb provides arms, officers, and purpose. The Bosniaks will become adversaries.

future_consequences.label: Croat republic pressure path
future_consequences.explanation: Choosing the Zagreb line records hrhb_political_goal as croat_republic, opening the Graz cooperation-collapse decision next, making the HVO central-Bosnia offensive rupture branch visible if its later conditions are met, opening the Vance-Owen pressure branch (Zagreb restrains Boban during the VOPP acceptance window) per Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 3 §§412-498, opening the Washington-track Zagreb ceasefire order (Feb 1994) that follows the Croat-Bosniak war collapse per Prlic Vol. 1 §§357-422, Vol. 2 §§556-590, and Vol. 2 §§600-680, and opening the August-September 1995 HV-HVO joint command coordination decision under the Susak-Tudjman channel per BB Vol. II Ch. 15 and Prlic Vol. 1 §§591-640.

future_consequences.label: Zagreb ceasefire-order path (February 1994)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the February 1994 Zagreb ceasefire-order decision: as Croatia's EU trajectory and US sanctions pressure tighten, Tudjman directs Boban via the Granic-Silajdzic channel to stand down HVO operations against ARBiH ahead of the Washington Agreement framework (Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§357-422 and Vol. 2 §§556-590; Vol. 2 §§600-680; Granic Vanjski poslovi (2005) Granic-Silajdzic channel; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts; US State Dept Christopher/Redman shuttle; Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II pp. 506-520).

future_consequences.label: Vance-Owen pressure path (early-mid 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the Vance-Owen pressure decision: Tudjman directs Boban to acknowledge the provincial-map framework as the operative territorial basis (signed at Geneva 2 January 1993), with restraint orders on HVO offensive operations during the VOPP acceptance window (Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 3 §§412-498, Appeals §§612-650; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlic Vol. 3 §§460-485; Vance-Owen Plan UN S/25221 Annex VII + UN S/25403 Annex II).

future_consequences.label: Vance-Owen acceptance decision (March 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the March 1993 Vance-Owen acceptance decision. The ten-province framework ratifies three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) under the decentralized Bosnia constitutional architecture; Tudjman's directive transmitted via the Granic-Susak channel aligns the Mostar Presidency with acceptance, and Mate Boban signed the agreed text at Athens on 25 March 1993 (Owen, Balkan Odyssey Ch. 4-5; Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§452-470; Vol. 3 §§412-498 — Tudjman Presidential Transcripts on HZ HB VOPP directive; UN S/25221 + UN S/25403 + UN S/25479; Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II Ch. 3-5). The Croat-republic line over-determines the historical accept posture — the diplomatic legitimization of three Croat-majority provinces is the value capture; the reject counterfactual breaks with Zagreb's directive and carries a Tudjman patron-confidence collapse plus an alliance break with RBiH on that branch.

future_consequences.label: Central Bosnia pocket defense decision (April-October 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line over-determines the April-October 1993 Central Bosnia pocket defense decision. After the Gornji Vakuf clashes (Jan 1993) escalated into the full ARBiH-HVO war through spring 1993, HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia (Blaškić) holds three encircled pockets — the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle, the Žepče exclave, and Mostar west bank — sustained via the Tudjman-Susak airbridge channel until the Washington Agreement of 18 March 1994. The Croat-republic line structurally aligns the HZ HB Presidency with defend_pocket as the documented historical posture: Zagreb's directive across spring 1993 was pocket-hold via the airbridge, not pocket-abandonment, breakout, or early federation. The federate_early counterfactual is structurally inconsistent with the Croat-republic pledge and carries the Tudjman patron-channel rupture cost (Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II April 1993-March 1994 chronology; ICTY Kordić & Čerkez IT-95-14/2-T §§465-650; ICTY Blaškić IT-95-14-T §§99-220; ICTY Prlić IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§591-640 and Vol. 3 §§412-498 — Tudjman-Susak airbridge correspondence). §3.6 STRICT: this consequence path remains operational (pocket defense / evacuation / breakout / early-federation) — the Lasva Valley sensitive history (Ahmici, Stupni Do, Vitez detention) stays canon-gated through the h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities + h8_mostar_bridge + hrhb_camp_exposure family slugs and MUST NOT surface as a downstream choice from any H6 option.

future_consequences.label: Owen-Stoltenberg response decision (Sep 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the September 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics response decision. The plan ratifies HZ HB as a constitutive ethnic republic with central-Bosnia and western Herzegovina territorial allocation favorable to Croat claims; Tudjman's directive transmitted via Susak aligns the Mostar Presidency with acceptance, and Mate Boban signed the framework on 20 September 1993 (Owen, Balkan Odyssey Ch. 7; Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§452-470; Vol. 3 §§412-498 — Tudjman Presidential Transcripts on HZ HB Owen-Stoltenberg directive). The Croat-republic line over-determines the historical accept posture — the diplomatic legitimization of Herceg-Bosna as a constitutive republic is the value capture; the reject counterfactual breaks with Zagreb's directive and carries a Tudjman patron-confidence collapse on this branch.

future_consequences.label: HRHB territorial-maximalist scope decision (summer 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the summer 1993 HRHB territorial-maximalist scope decision at the moment of peak HZ HB territorial reach (Mostar west bank consolidated 9 May 1993; Central Bosnia Vitez/Busovača/Kiseljak triangle + Žepče exclave; Herzegovina core). The Croat-republic line over-determines acceptance of the pragmatic_maximum historical default — the Tudjman-Šušak scope-restraint channel was operative across spring-summer 1993 (Prlić IT-04-74-T Vol. 3 §§412-498 Tudjman Presidential Transcripts; Prlić Appeals §§601-650 on the 1939 Banovina template). The expansive_conquest counterfactual ruptures the Tudjman scope-restraint channel and triggers UNSCR triple-sanctions-equivalent international recoil; the maximalist_with_serb_alliance counterfactual is the maximum-cost option set, formalizing the Boban-Karadžić Graz 6 May 1992 axis against Sarajevo's central-Bosnia residual at the cost of Federation-track foreclosure and Tudjman patron-confidence collapse; the minimum_consolidation counterfactual abandons the central-Bosnia pockets diplomatically and opens the Federation-track early at the cost of the Croat-nationalist faction revolt inside HZ HB. §3.6 STRICT: this consequence path authors only the diplomatic-scope posture decision — the Lašva Valley sensitive history (Ahmici, Stupni Do, Vitez detention, Heliodrom/Dretelj/Gabela detention camps, Stari Most destruction) stays canon-gated through the h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities + h8_mostar_bridge + hrhb_camp_exposure + hrhb_detention_camp_exposure + hrhb_mostar_bridge_destruction_1993 family slugs per src/sim/events/event_families.ts RING3_SENSITIVE_FAMILIES and MUST NOT surface as a downstream choice from any H40 option.

future_consequences.label: Federation backchannel overture decision (Oct-Dec 1993)
future_consequences.explanation: Even the Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the October-December 1993 federation backchannel overture decision sitting BEFORE H4 (February 1994 Zagreb-ordered HVO ceasefire, war_1994.json turn 95-103) and H9 (March 1994 Washington Agreement formal signature, war_1994.json turn 102). Tudjman's strategic recalculation after the September 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg failure, the central-Bosnia territorial pressure from the ARBiH September-October 1993 counter-offensive, and the tightening US sanctions pressure on Croatia produced a backchannel federation overture window operationalized through Galbraith (US Ambassador to Zagreb from 28 June 1993), Swoboda (German CD foreign-policy office), and Holbrooke (Bonn-Geneva shuttle from September 1993). The Croat-republic line raises the political cost of extend_federation_overture relative to the Croat-nationalist faction inside HZ HB but does not foreclose the trigger: Tudjman's directive transmitted via the Susak channel still presses the Mostar Presidency to record a written posture on the federation backchannel three months ahead of the formal Washington signature (Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II 1993-94 Federation prelude pp. 451-455 + Ch. 12; Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 2 §§556-590 + Vol. 3 §§120-200; Galbraith, The Pact chs. 4-5; Holbrooke, To End a War chs. 3-5; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts federation-overture set). H30 is DISTINCT from H4 (`zagreb_orders_hrhb_ceasefire`, Feb 1994 — Zagreb-ordered HVO ceasefire under US sanctions pressure preceding Washington) and from H9 (`hrhb_washington_agreement_1994`, March 1994 — formal Washington Agreement signature 1+18 March 1994 + Vienna Framework 26 March 1994): H30 captures the BACKCHANNEL WINDOW BEFORE both. §3.6 STRICT: any future `csq_hrhb_federation_overture_*` row consuming this row's outcomes MUST NOT re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, civilian-targeting, hostage-taking, paramilitary deployment, ethnic-targeting, or any sensitive-act response option; the Lasva Valley sensitive history (Ahmici, Stupni Do, Vitez detention, Heliodrom/Dretelj/Gabela detention camps, Stari Most destruction) stays canon-gated through h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities + h8_mostar_bridge + hrhb_camp_exposure + hrhb_detention_camp_exposure + hrhb_mostar_bridge_destruction_1993 family slugs per src/sim/events/event_families.ts RING3_SENSITIVE_FAMILIES.

future_consequences.label: Washington Agreement acceptance path (March 1994)
future_consequences.explanation: Even the Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the March 1994 Washington Agreement decision: U.S. sanctions pressure on Croatia transmitted via Tudjman makes the Washington acceptance event reachable once turn ~102 arrives, regardless of which H1 line the HZ HB Presidency took in 1992 (Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§452-470, Vol. 3 §§120-200).

future_consequences.label: Federation Army integration depth decision (mid-1994)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to face the mid-1994 Federation Army (HVOBiH / VFBiH) integration depth decision following the Washington Agreement of 1 + 18 March 1994 and the Vienna Framework of 26 March 1994. Six months after the Federation Army's paper establishment, US Defense Department liaison and the embassy's defense attaché press the Mostar Presidency for a written posture on HVO command-integration depth; HVO formations continue to answer through the Mostar Defence Department and the Zagreb-Susak channel rather than the Federation general staff (BB Vol. II pp. 451-455 + Ch. 12; Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§452-470 + Vol. 3 §§120-200; Tudjman-Susak correspondence excerpts admitted at Prlic Vol. 3; ICRC field reports; US embassy archived reporting Christopher / Galbraith / Redman channels). The Croat-republic line over-determines acceptance of the parallel-commands historical default — Zagreb's preference for retaining the HVO parallel-command lever inside the Federation paper architecture is structurally consistent with the 1992 Zagreb-aligned pledge.

future_consequences.label: Contact Group 51/49 response decision (July 1994)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line reaches the Contact Group 51:49 framework decision presented in early July 1994. With the Washington Agreement of 1+18 March 1994 already in place and HR HB operating inside the Federation framework (Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§452-470), Tudjman directs Boban-successor leadership to accept the Contact Group map — Croatia's EU trajectory and US sanctions pressure transmit through Zagreb to align HR HB with the Federation/RS dual-entity territorial settlement. The HZ HB Presidency faces the historical accept (already in Federation March 1994) vs counterfactual reject posture decision; the reject counterfactual breaks the Federation alliance and carries a patron-confidence collapse from Zagreb (Contact Group proposal, July 1994; Holbrooke To End a War Ch. 5; UNSCR 942 of 23 September 1994; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlic Vol. 3).

future_consequences.label: HV-HVO joint command coordination decision (August-September 1995)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line carries the cleanest path into the August-September 1995 HV-HVO joint command coordination decision. On 4 August 1995 — the opening day of Operation Storm — HV Guards Brigades crossed the international border to operate openly inside Bosnia-Herzegovina alongside HVO units, and the September Mistral 2 axis (Sipovo, Mrkonjic Grad, Jajce, 8-13 September 1995) was prosecuted under combined HV-HVO command via the Susak-Tudjman-Boban-successor channel (BB Vol. II Ch. 15; Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§591-640 and Vol. 3; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlic Vol. 3; ICTY Gotovina et al. IT-06-90 Trial and Appeals Judgments; Holbrooke To End a War Ch. 9-11). The Zagreb-aligned line minimizes the political cost of accepting HV operational direction.

future_consequences.label: Dayton acceptance decision (November-December 1995)
future_consequences.explanation: The Zagreb-aligned Croat-republic line is structurally bound to reach the Dayton General Framework Agreement decision (initialed 21 November 1995; signed Paris 14 December 1995; UN S/1995/999; UN S/RES/1031 of 15 December 1995). HR HB acts through the Federation channel established by the Washington Agreement (1 March 1994; Prlić IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§591-620); Annex 4 (BiH Constitution) ratifies Croat constitutive-nation status inside the Federation entity. The post-Storm / Mistral-2 HV-HVO-ARBiH coalition position (Krajina recovered; western and central Bosnia favorable) maximizes Zagreb's leverage over Zubak (HR HB President from 5 August 1994 under Federation reform) and binds the HR HB delegation to ratification through the Croatian delegation channel (Prlić IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§591-640; Holbrooke To End a War; Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3).

response_options.label: United front with ARBiH
response_options.description: We are Croats and Bosnians. Our fight is against Greater Serbia, alongside our allies. Zagreb will be furious. Tudjman may cut support. But the combined front against the VRS will be formidable.

future_consequences.label: United-front branch
future_consequences.explanation: Choosing the united-front line records hrhb_political_goal as united_front, opening the Graz cooperation-collapse decision next (where the HZ HB Presidency can act to suppress local frictions), making the joint-operations and early-Federation branches visible if their later conditions are met, opening the Vance-Owen pressure branch (Tudjman still applies patron pressure on the HZ HB Presidency during the VOPP window, even on the united-front line) per Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 3 §§412-498, and opening the February 1994 Zagreb ceasefire-order decision that follows the Washington track (Prlic Vol. 1 §§357-422 and Vol. 2 §§556-590, Vol. 2 §§600-680; Granic-Silajdzic channel). Cost floor: Zagreb withdraws officer secondments, fuel, and ammunition support, modeled as a 0.85 equipment_quality_modifier (Prlic Vol. 2 §§220-260).

future_consequences.label: Zagreb ceasefire-order path (February 1994)

The united-front posture raises the political cost of patron-direction acknowledgement but does not foreclose the trigger (Prlic IT-04-74 Vol. 1 §§357-422 and Vol. 2 §§556-590, Vol. 2 §§600-680; Granic Vanjski poslovi (2005) Granic-Silajdzic channel; US State Dept Christopher/Redman shuttle; Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II pp. 506-520).

title: UN Arms Embargo Strangles Bosnia
narrative: The UN arms embargo, originally imposed on all of Yugoslavia, disproportionately impacts the fledgling Bosnian government. While the VRS inherits vast JNA stockpiles and the HVO receives supplies from Croatia, the ARBiH faces severe weapons shortages across all fronts.

effects.text: The UN arms embargo leaves the ARBiH critically short of weapons and ammunition.

title: Graz and the Frictions of Cooperation
narrative: Karadzic and Boban have met in Graz. The 6 May 1992 joint statement records a Croat-Serb understanding on the territorial organization of Bosnia-Herzegovina — partition lines that leave only residual central-Bosnia ground for Sarajevo. The HVO 4th Brigade still holds the Mostar line against the JNA/VRS; in Prozor, Novi Travnik, and Vitez, local HVO commanders begin asserting HZ HB jurisdiction over checkpoints, factories, and municipal command. Zagreb's transcripts read Graz as compatible with the HZ HB project, but with diplomatic risk. The political files require a posture: accept the local frictions as the visible cost of separate trajectories, or have the Presidency intervene at command level to suppress them and preserve the joint anti-VRS framework.

effect.text: The HZ HB Presidency records its posture toward the Graz framework and the summer-1992 local frictions.

title: Battle of the Barracks — Sarajevo
narrative: TDF units and Green Berets storm JNA barracks across Sarajevo. The Maršal Tito barracks and Viktor Bubanj complex are seized after fierce fighting. Tanks, APCs, and artillery pieces are captured — the first heavy weapons in ARBiH hands. JNA soldiers are taken prisoner. Belgrade vows retaliation.

In the chaos, TDF forces seize the barracks complex with its armored vehicles and artillery depot. Over 50 JNA soldiers are killed — the bloodiest barracks seizure in Bosnia. narrative: ARBiH forces seize the JNA barracks in Zenica, capturing artillery pieces and ammunition stores. The Zenica garrison, weakened by Bosniak desertions, offers limited resistance. The captured equipment is distributed to 3rd Corps formations defending central Bosnia.

title: Siege of Sarajevo Intensifies
narrative: The SRK tightens its grip around Sarajevo as artillery bombardment from surrounding hills intensifies. The city's 350,000 residents face daily shelling, sniper fire, and the severing of water and electricity supplies. The siege becomes the longest in modern European warfare.

effect.text: Sarajevo is encircled. The SRK begins systematic bombardment from positions on the surrounding hills.

title: JNA Forces Begin Withdrawal from Bosnia
narrative: The Yugoslav People's Army formally announces its withdrawal from Bosnia-Herzegovina. In practice, Bosnian Serb personnel simply change insignia, and massive quantities of heavy weapons, ammunition depots, and military infrastructure are transferred directly to the newly formed VRS.

title: Mostar Liberated
narrative: Joint HVO-ARBiH forces have pushed the JNA out of Mostar. The city is free — but the question of who controls it is already causing friction between your allies. The east bank is mostly Bosniak. The west bank is mostly Croat. The liberation was shared. The city may not be.

narrative: Under the command of Naser Oric, Bosniak forces in the Drina Valley consolidate a defensive perimeter around Srebrenica. Despite being vastly outgunned, local TDF fighters and volunteers launch raids on surrounding VRS positions, establishing a tenuous enclave that shelters tens of thousands of displaced civilians.

title: Operation Circle: The Gorazde Pocket Holds
narrative: The 1st and 31st Drina Strike Brigades of the ARBiH launch Operation Circle, a counteroffensive to push VRS forces out of Gorazde's eastern approaches. After weeks of fighting through August, the operation succeeds in consolidating the enclave's perimeter, securing outlying settlements and establishing a defensible pocket. Gorazde — the largest Bosniak-held enclave in the Drina valley — will endure under siege for the remainder of the war, but it will not fall.

title: Sarajevo Records Its Officer Corps Posture
narrative: ARBiH command at the Sarajevo HQ records its posture toward minority retention. The wartime army still carries substantial Serb and Croat officers and recruits — Gen. Jovan Divjak holds Deputy Commander at HQ Sarajevo, mixed-ethnicity units anchor the city's defense, and the civic-republic platform makes multi-ethnic service a structural foundation of state legitimacy. A Bosniak-nationalist faction inside the SDA presses for ethnic vetting and purges. President Izetbegović and the General Staff weigh the response: retain the multi-ethnic officer corps and recruitment pool (the documented historical posture); execute a gradual purge over several months; mandate immediate ethnic vetting and dismissal; or move to federated single-ethnicity unit structures as a compromise. The decision shapes who fights for the republic, who funds it, and what civic claim the state can advance at the diplomatic table.

effect.text: Sarajevo records its minority-retention posture for the ARBiH officer corps and recruitment pool.

source_note: The multi-ethnic composition of the ARBiH was a defining structural feature of the wartime Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The army retained substantial Serb and Croat officer corps and recruits throughout the war: Gen. Jovan Divjak (Serb, JNA-trained) served as Deputy Commander of the Sarajevo HQ from April 1992 through the war's end (memoir 'Sarajevo, Mon Amour' Buchet/Chastel 2004 + ARBiH command records); Stjepan Šiber (Croat) served as Deputy Commander General Staff; mixed-ethnicity units operated in Sarajevo defense, the Tuzla cantonment, and the Mostar east-bank defense. The civic-republic platform documented at B1 (`rbih_state_identity`) makes multi-ethnic officer/recruit retention a structural foundation of state legitimacy — Izetbegović and the General Staff resisted internal Bosniak-nationalist pressure for ethnic purges throughout the war. The documented historical posture is retain_minorities: no formal ethnic vetting, no institutional purge campaign, sustained recognition of minority service across the officer corps and recruitment base. Sources: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II (CIA Office of Russian and European Analysis 2002) chs. on ARBiH composition + 1st Corps Sarajevo defense + General Staff structure; ICTY context for Sarajevo defense organization (Galić IT-98-29-T, Dragomir Milošević IT-98-29/1-T, Karadžić IT-95-5/18-T trial records on ARBiH 1st Corps and Sarajevo HQ command structure); Jovan Divjak, 'Sarajevo, Mon Amour' (Buchet/Chastel 2004) — Divjak's Serb-ethnic ARBiH service as Deputy Commander Sarajevo HQ from April 1992; Marko Attila Hoare, 'How Bosnia Armed' (Saqi 2004) on the civic-republic posture preserving minority service through the war; ARBiH command records and General Staff order-of-battle documentation. §3.6 forward-looking guard (STRICT — identity-coupled lane): any future `csq_rbih_minority_*` row consuming this row's outcomes MUST NOT re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, ethnic-targeting, paramilitary-deployment, hostage-taking, civilian-targeting, or any sensitive-act response option. The minority-retention decision is a CONSTITUTIONAL-POLITICAL crisis lane (officer-corps composition; recruitment-pool ethnic policy; civic-republic legitimacy posture) — NOT operational ethnic-targeting. Even the purge counterfactuals (gradual_purge / mandatory_purge) are modeled as COHESION + LEGITIMACY + RECRUITMENT costs (internal_cohesion penalty, international_standing penalty, alliance_change penalty, recruitment_modifier penalty, patron_pressure spike) — NOT as atrocity rewards, NOT as ethnic-cleansing enabling, NOT as forced-displacement triggers. Any associated atrocity surfaces (the Drina-valley cleansing, central-Bosnia detention camps, Sarajevo siege fires, Goražde enclave operations, Stupni Do, Mostar siege) remain canon-gated through their existing event surfaces (drina_valley_ethnic_cleansing_1992, concentration_camps_revealed_1992, h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities, h8_mostar_bridge family slugs). The cost-floor topology reflects the civic-legitimacy stakes: retain_minorities (historical) carries POSITIVE multi-ethnic boosts (internal_cohesion +5, international_standing +15, alliance_change +0.05, recruitment_modifier 1.05x for 12 turns capturing the multi-ethnic recruitment pool expansion, negotiating_leverage +5); gradual_purge (counterfactual) carries moderate punitive costs (internal_cohesion -15, international_standing -10, alliance_change -0.05, negotiating_leverage -10); mandatory_purge (counterfactual, maximum punitive) carries severe costs (internal_cohesion -25, international_standing -30, alliance_change -0.15, recruitment_modifier 0.85x for 8 turns, patron_pressure +20 capturing US/EU recoil); federated_units (counterfactual, intermediate compromise) carries moderate mixed costs (internal_cohesion -10, alliance_change +0.05 modest Federation-track alignment, negotiating_leverage +5). staff_assessment: The General Staff and President Izetbegović align on retain_minorities as the documented historical posture: the civic-republic platform's commitment to equal citizenship structurally requires multi-ethnic officer retention, and the operational reality — Divjak at Sarajevo HQ, Šiber on the General Staff, mixed-ethnicity units anchoring the defense of Sarajevo and central Bosnia — makes ethnic purges institutionally costly and diplomatically suicidal. The internal SDA-nationalist faction pressing for purges loses the institutional argument because the alternative (mandatory_purge) collapses three lanes simultaneously: international standing (US/EU recoil; Western diplomatic exposure), the Federation track (the civic platform underwrites the Washington Agreement framework), and the recruitment pool (Bosniak-only constriction in a war already manpower-stretched). The gradual_purge counterfactual occupies the middle band — slower visible damage but still cumulative civic-legitimacy and Federation-track costs. The federated_units counterfactual is the intermediate compromise: single-ethnicity unit structures preserve some institutional coherence at the cost of unified ARBiH command and the civic claim — modest Federation-track alignment but the civic-republic posture weakens.
trigger_evidence: ARBiH command at HQ Sarajevo carries substantial Serb and Croat officer presence (Divjak, Šiber, multiple mixed-ethnicity units).
The SDA Bosniak-nationalist faction is pressing the Presidency for ethnic vetting and purges.
The civic-republic platform recorded at B1 (rbih_state_identity) makes the minority-retention posture a structural foundation of state legitimacy that must be explicitly declared.

response_options.label: Retain the multi-ethnic officer corps
response_options.description: Reject the SDA-nationalist pressure for ethnic vetting. Keep Divjak at Sarajevo HQ, Šiber on the General Staff, and the mixed-ethnicity units intact. The civic-republic platform is preserved at the institutional level. Western diplomatic standing rises; the Federation-track alignment with HRHB strengthens; the multi-ethnic recruitment pool expands. The SDA-nationalist faction grumbles but loses the institutional argument.

response_options.label: Execute a gradual ethnic purge
response_options.description: Initiate a slow-motion ethnic vetting program. Minority officers retain their commissions on paper but are rotated to non-command staff roles; Serb and Croat recruits face informal screening at induction. The civic-republic platform erodes by attrition rather than rupture. Western diplomatic exposure is moderated but cumulative; the Federation-track alignment with HRHB weakens; the SDA-nationalist faction is partly mollified.

response_options.label: Mandate immediate ethnic vetting and dismissal
response_options.description: Issue a Presidency directive dismissing Serb and Croat officers from command roles. Divjak is removed from Sarajevo HQ; Šiber is sidelined from the General Staff; mixed-ethnicity units are restructured along single-ethnicity lines. The civic-republic platform collapses at the institutional level. Western patrons recoil (US/EU push back explicitly); the Federation-track alignment with HRHB ruptures; the multi-ethnic recruitment pool constricts to a Bosniak-only base; the SDA-nationalist faction is satisfied but the diplomatic and institutional damage is severe and durable.

response_options.label: Move to federated single-ethnicity units
response_options.description: Reorganize ARBiH into federated single-ethnicity unit structures. Bosniak units, Serb units, and Croat units operate under unified command but with ethnic separation at the brigade level. The civic-republic posture weakens at the operational level but a Federation-style federated army shell is preserved on paper. The Federation-track alignment with HRHB modestly strengthens (institutional compatibility); the civic-republic claim takes a moderate hit; internal cohesion suffers from the structural reorganization mid-war.

RS.headline: Sarajevo affirms multi-ethnic ARBiH composition
RS.body: ARBiH command at HQ Sarajevo declares retention of the Serb and Croat officer corps and the multi-ethnic recruitment pool. Pale reads the declaration as a civic-legitimacy reinforcement against partition claims; the Divjak-at-Sarajevo-HQ posture remains intact.

HRHB.headline: ARBiH keeps Croat officers and recruits
HRHB.body: Sarajevo's command structure preserves multi-ethnic composition. Mostar reads the Federation-track signal: the civic platform that would underwrite a future Washington-track alignment with HRHB holds at the institutional level.

RS.headline: Sarajevo begins quiet ethnic vetting
RS.body: ARBiH minority officers are rotated to non-command staff roles. Pale reads the slow erosion of Sarajevo's civic claim — the SDA-nationalist faction is gaining ground even without a formal purge directive.

HRHB.headline: Croat officers sidelined in ARBiH command
HRHB.body: Sarajevo begins gradual ethnic vetting at the operational level. Mostar reads the Federation-track weakening: the civic platform that would underwrite a unified army is eroding by attrition.

RS.headline: Sarajevo mandates ethnic dismissal in ARBiH
RS.body: ARBiH Presidency directive dismisses Serb and Croat officers from command roles. Divjak removed from HQ Sarajevo. Pale reads the civic-republic collapse — Sarajevo can no longer credibly claim the legitimacy ground at the diplomatic table.

HRHB.headline: ARBiH purges Croat officers from command
HRHB.body: Sarajevo's mandatory ethnic vetting directive removes Croat officers from ARBiH command. Mostar reads the Federation-track rupture — the civic platform that would underwrite the Washington framework collapses at the institutional level.

RS.headline: Sarajevo restructures ARBiH into ethnic federated units
RS.body: ARBiH reorganizes into federated single-ethnicity brigade structures under unified command. Pale reads the partial concession to ethnic separation logic — the civic-republic claim is weakening at the operational level.

HRHB.headline: ARBiH adopts federated single-ethnicity structure
HRHB.body: Sarajevo reorganizes ARBiH into single-ethnicity brigades under unified command. Mostar reads the Federation-track compatibility — the institutional shell is more amenable to a future HVO-ARBiH joint Federation army architecture.

title: Jajce Falls to VRS Forces
narrative: The strategic town of Jajce in central Bosnia falls to the VRS after a prolonged siege. The loss is a major blow to both the ARBiH and HVO, who blame each other for failing to coordinate the defense. Tens of thousands of civilians flee westward, and recriminations between the two forces deepen the growing rift.
